image_description: A close-up shot of a green snake, identified as a green mamba, coiled around a brown branch. The head is in sharp focus, showing detailed scales and a dark eye. The body curves behind the head, displaying bright green coloration with some yellow undertones on the ventral side. The background is a soft, out-of-focus dark green/black.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is pale yellow-green to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the coiled body shows a lighter, yellowish-green hue, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Uniform green coloration with no patterning.

This suggests it might be a juvenile or a different species entirely (e.g., Green Tree Python or Vine Snake).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scales are smooth and highly glossy with a reflective surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is laterally compressed, adapted for arboreal locomotion.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body appears more cylindrical than laterally compressed. Laterally compressed bodies usually look thinner from the top-down view seen here; this snake retains significant girth.
The tail tip is not visible in the frame; it is occluded by the coiling and image cropping.
